items.summary: Security disposition: evidence_needed. Risk severity: high for go-live, new public exposure, and security-sensitive releases; conditional for ordinary reversible growth that adds no credentials, permissions, dependencies, data collection, cross-site behavior, or unsupported claims. Evidence: the security fleet-doctor has no run or findings, and operations deploy, uptime, and error sweeps have no results. Authentication and access boundaries, secrets handling, container/runtime isolation, release and deployment controls, dependency provenance, complete TLS controls, data exposure, monitoring and incident readiness, and security.txt/disclosure readiness therefore remain unknown. HTTPS checks and the absence of TLS certificates expiring within 30 days do not establish complete TLS assurance. Compliance is technical-only: 36 pass, 19 fail, and 6 unknown, with open banner, consent, GA4, privacy, and terms findings; data quality is not security evidence. Exact decision: keep new public exposure, go-live, and security-sensitive releases blocked; retain the existing read-only security evidence matrix; do not create duplicate telemetry, proposals, deployments, credential or permission changes, dependency additions, configuration changes, or external outreach. Ordinary reversible growth may proceed only within the stated boundaries. No clean bill of health or certification is claimed.

Retain the current containment decision and reject duplicate security work this cycle. The existing fleet security evidence work remains the correct next action: use authorized metadata and retained artifacts to document authentication and access boundaries, secrets exposure, runtime isolation, release controls, dependency and supply-chain provenance, TLS, data exposure, monitoring and incident signals, incident readiness, and disclosure readiness. Preserve unknowns, record timestamps, affected scope, owners, severity, and release implications, and do not clear any gate without dated evidence and an owner-approved disposition.
